page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%, alongside poor single-threaded gzip compression. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, with Passmark CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scores all placing in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests also demonstrate average throughput, reaching 75.86 GB/sec for large block reads and 55.65 GB/sec for large block writes.

Given its hardware profile, the ecs.sn2.3xlarge offers moderate resource density and balanced compute-to-memory ratios, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads that can leverage parallel execution rather than raw single-threaded speed. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, Redis database operations, and moderate software compilation tasks. It is less suitable for single-threaded processing or large-scale LLM inference.
